hens_rule_text: Up to 6 chickens and/or domestic fowl over 6 months old (plus up to 6 more under 6 months old) per property; no permit needed.
permit_notes: No special permit required to keep chickens or domestic fowl; owners must follow sanitation and setback standards in the code.
setback_notes: Coops should be placed at least 10 ft from property lines; not stated as distance from a neighbor's dwelling specifically.
coop_rules: Standards cover sanitation and coop placement under the urban animal keeping rules; specific coop size limits were not found in the sources checked.
zoning_notes: Roosters, geese, peacocks and turkeys are prohibited. Domestic fowl (quail, pheasants, ducks, pigeons, doves) are allowed under the same standards as chickens.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Eugene Code 9.5250, Urban Animal Keeping Standards (municipal.codes)
BackYard Chickens: Eugene Oregon Chicken Ordinance

research_notes: Facts come from a WebSearch extract that names and quotes Eugene Code 9.5250 (flock limits by age, rooster/goose/peacock/turkey ban, 10 ft coop setback, no permit); the municipal.codes page itself returned a 403 to direct fetch, so the full section text was not independently read and slaughter is unaddressed in the extract.
